page: Google Cloud Platform ct5p-hightpu-4t is a specialized accelerator platform engineered for compute-heavy artificial intelligence and numerical computing tasks. At its core, the instance integrates 4 Google TPU v5p chips featuring a combined 380 GB of high-bandwidth tensor processing memory. The host subsystem is powered by an x86_64 architecture with 208 dedicated vCPUs and 448 GB of system memory, which allocates approximately 2.15 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with the server, necessitating network storage attachments to handle operating system images, training data, and checkpoint logs.

The primary performance profile of ct5p-hightpu-4t centers on matrix multiplication throughput and tensor operations powered by the TPU v5p accelerators. The 380 GB pool of accelerator memory accommodates substantial parameter counts and batch sizes without requiring aggressive memory offloading to the host. Concurrently, the 208 dedicated host vCPUs and 448 GB host RAM ensure that data ingest pipelines, tokenization, augmentation, and distributed coordination execute without creating significant processing bottlenecks for the accelerators.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the platform delivers high compute density tailored for specialized tensor mathematics rather than general-purpose hosting. The absence of onboard NVMe storage represents an operational tradeoff, shifting I/O responsibilities to network-attached block or object storage architectures. ct5p-hightpu-4t is best suited for resource-intensive workloads such as large-scale deep learning training, foundation model fine-tuning, high-throughput transformer inference, and large matrix-driven scientific simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform ct5p-hightpu-4t is an accelerator-specialized instance designed for demanding machine learning and high-performance computing pipelines. Powered by an x86_64 host platform, it provisions 208 dedicated vCPUs alongside 448 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 2.15 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is provided by 4 Google TPU v5p chips, contributing a combined total of 380 GB of accelerator memory for high-capacity tensor operations and complex distributed training loops. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for datasets, model checkpoints, and system files. With dedicated compute cores and high accelerator memory capacity, the instance maximizes operational efficiency by reducing data transfer bottlenecks between host memory and accelerator memory. Google Cloud Platform ct5p-hightpu-4t is purpose-built for workloads including large language model training, multi-modal neural network fine-tuning, complex transformer inference, and highly parallel matrix-based scientific computations.
